problem.text: What is the units digit of $13^{2003}$?

steps.title: Where to start: look for a pattern in the units digits
steps.body: $13^{2003}$ is far too big to compute, but we only need its last digit. The units digit of a product depends only on the units digits of the factors, so we can track just the last digit of each power of $13$ and look for a repeat.

your_turn.prompt: Find the units digits of $13^1$, $13^2$, $13^3$, $13^4$ and $13^5$.
your_turn.answer: $3, 9, 7, 1, 3$. Each is the previous digit times $3$, keeping only the last digit.

steps.title: The cycle has length $4$
steps.body: Once the units digit returns to $3$ at $13^5$, the whole pattern $3, 9, 7, 1$ repeats. So exponents that differ by a multiple of $4$ give the same units digit, and only the remainder of the exponent when divided by $4$ matters.

your_turn.prompt: What is the remainder when $2003$ is divided by $4$?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Since $2003$ leaves remainder $3$, $13^{2003}$ has the same units digit as $13^3$, which is the third digit in the cycle $3, 9, 7, 1$. The units digit is $7$. The answer is **(C)** $7$.
